newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada upholds arrest warrant of Thai banker.
newsitem.headline: Canada upholds arrest warrant of Thai banker.

text.p: A Canadian judge on Wednesday upheld the arrest warrant for a former Thai bank official accused of embezzlement, but it remained unclear when proceedings to extradite him to Thailand could begin.
British Columbia Supreme Court Justice Frank Maczko rejected a petition from Rakesh Saxena, former treasury adviser to the Bangkok Bank of Commerce, to have his original arrest warrant quashed.

Canadian and Thai police arrested Saxena last July at the Whistler mountain resort near Vancouver. An Indian citizen and former resident of Thailand, Saxena is accused of colluding with a group of Bangkok Bank of Commerce executives to embezzle about $65 million.

The judge said on Wednesday the warrant met the requirements of extradition treaties between Canada and Thailand. "I find the warrant was valid and made with the necessary jurisdiction," Maczko said in the ruling.
Saxena's lawyer, Winton Derby, had argued the original arrest warrant against Saxena was improperly issued because no prosecution against him had been launched in Thailand.

Derby said on Wednesday he planned an immediate appeal of the ruling and sought to have the extradition hearing delayed. Deborah Strachan, a Canadian prosecutor representing Thailand in the case, said Thailand would seek to have Saxena's appeal quashed and opposed an adjournment.
Maczko said he would put the case on hold until Monday to give them time to take the matter to the British Columbia Court of Appeal. It was not clear whether the appeal court would accept the case.

Until the appeal court acts, Maczko said he would not postpone the much-delayed extradition case in his court. Noting the many months in delays, he said extradition matters were intended to be handled expeditiously.

The Thai government took over the Bangkok bank a year ago after a public run on deposits sparked by news it was saddled with about $2.7 billion in bad loans. The run was triggered by opposition party charges about the bad loans and the case took on political overtones. Since Saxena's arrest, he has been named in a second similar case along with Saudi tycoon Adnan Khashoggi.
